title: Antipasto platter
skill: A cold platter that holds below 41°F

notes.text: Build two platters: one out, one in the fridge to swap in at the 1-hour mark.

move.title: Cold, and kept that way
move.body: An Italian antipasto is the table before the meal: cured beef, cheeses, marinated vegetables, olives, and a chopped salad, set out for guests to help themselves. This is the unit's mastery week. The cutting is quick; the skill is keeping every perishable item at 41°F or below for as long as it's out.

why.title: Cold from start to finish
why.body: Sliced meats and soft cheeses support bacterial growth once they warm past 41°F. A platter built from cold ingredients on a chilled tray, set on ice, starts cold and stays there. Building it at room temperature uses up the safe window before guests arrive.

why.title: Ice under, not on
why.body: A sheet pan or roasting pan of ice under the platter pulls heat out of everything resting on it. Ice on the food itself waters it down and makes cheese slick.

why.title: Small and refilled
why.body: A small platter refilled from the fridge holds colder than one big one left out, and nothing that has sat out mixes with fresh food. The last refill goes out no later than the 2-hour mark of the first.

why.title: The 2-hour rule
why.body: Perishable food off ice goes back in the fridge or the bin within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F. On ice, with a thermometer reading 41°F or below, it can stay out longer, but check it every 30 minutes and write the readings down.

why.title: Salad dressed at service
why.body: The chopped salad holds crisp on ice for hours undressed. Dressed, it wilts in under an hour, so it's tossed in small amounts as it's refilled.

wrong.sign: The thermometer in the mozzarella reads 45°F
wrong.fix: Swap that plate for a fresh one from the fridge and add ice under the tray. Discard what came off if it's been out more than 2 hours.

wrong.sign: The ice has melted into a puddle
wrong.fix: Drain the tray and refill it. Use a deeper pan, or a layer of ice packs under loose ice.
It came out too early. Keep it in the fridge until the platter is built, and slice it cold.
It was dressed too early. Dress only what's going out.

quiz.q: What temperature must a cold platter stay at or below?
quiz.explain: The cold-holding limit in the FDA Food Code.
It cools without watering anything down.

quiz.q: How long can perishable food sit out off ice?
quiz.explain: Then it goes back in the fridge or the bin.

quiz.q: Why refill a small platter rather than set out a big one?
choices: Small batches stay colder and nothing old mixes with fresh
quiz.explain: Fresh food from the fridge replaces what's been out.

ingredients.prep: small balls, or a ball cut in ¾-inch cubes

substitutions.note: Slice and toast gluten-free bread, and keep it in its own basket so it doesn't pick up crumbs.

steps.text: Put the serving platter in the freezer, and freeze a sheet pan of water or a tray of ice packs for the ice bed.
Whisk the vinegar, mustard, oregano, salt, and pepper until the salt dissolves, then whisk in the oil. Refrigerate it.
Rinse the chickpeas. Cut the romaine into ¾-inch squares, seed and dice the tomatoes at ⅜ inch, and mince the onion. Combine, undressed, and refrigerate.
Straight from the fridge, slice the beef salami ⅛ inch thick and cut the provolone into ¾-inch batons. Keep everything cold until the platter is out of the freezer.
Drain the artichokes, peppers, and olives in the colander and pat the peppers dry. Cut the peppers into 2-cm strips.
Slice the baguette ⅜ inch thick on a bias.
Set the frozen tray under the cold platter. Fan the beef salami, fold the bresaola into loose ribbons, and group the cheeses, vegetables, and olives in sections.
steps.look: Groups of each item, bread in a basket beside it, not on the ice.

steps.text: Push the thermometer into a mozzarella ball. Serve only when it reads 41°F or below, and write down the time.
Toss a third of the salad with a third of the dressing and set it out in a bowl over ice.
Every 30 minutes, probe the mozzarella and log the reading. Refill from the fridge on a fresh plate rather than topping up the old one.
At 2 hours, or any reading above 41°F, take the platter in. Refrigerate what stayed on ice and read 41°F or below; discard the rest.
